changed.title: Small cases only: some n by n bipartite graph, n at least 3, needs more than 2n - 4 AND/OR gates of fan-in two beyond its complement's to be represented
changed.statement: ¬ (∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), 3 ≤ n → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v => !A u v) s → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + (2 * n - 4)))
changed.unlocks: whether some graph costs more than its complement plus 2n - 4, for the NOT-gate transfer line
changed.context: Small cases only. Truth open; the statement it negates is posted beside it. An answer is one n by n graph, n at least 3, with an AND/OR circuit of s gates for its complement and a proof that no AND/OR circuit of at most s + 2n - 4 gates represents it. Our tables at sides 3 and 4 (computed, not checked) put the largest gap at exactly 2n - 4, so a break needs side 5 or more. A break-it of its own cannot exist: this row is itself the break of the statement beside it.

changed.title: Majority of 7 bits (at least 4 on): at most 21 AND, OR, NOT gates, none dead, a NOT on a gate
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack 7 C ∧ C.size ≤ 21 ∧ (∀ x : Fin 7 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = decide (4 ≤ (List.ofFn x).count true)) ∧ (∀ j < C.size, C.output = 7 + j ∨ ∃ i < C.size, j < i ∧ 7 + j ∈ (C.gates.getD i ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, []⟩).inputs) ∧ (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not → 7 ≤ g.inputs.headD 0 → (C.gates.getD (g.inputs.headD 0 - 7) ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, []⟩).op ≠ PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) ∧ (∃ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧ 7 ≤ g.inputs.headD 0)
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate can be at work at the best known size for this function
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, at most two earlier wires each; wires 0 to 6 the inputs, gate j writes wire 7+j) and the output wire, judged on every input. 21 is the size of the best AND/OR circuit the checker has accepted, so a yes is a circuit with a NOT at work that ties it. A circuit where the NOT and the gate reading it can be deleted and the rest is still right satisfies this row and shows nothing; say whether yours survives that deletion. So does a NOT-free circuit three gates smaller with one gate rewritten through NOTs; say if yours is one.
changed.sketch: A circuit three gates below our NOT-free bar also answers this; a calibration of our constructions, no claim attached either way. Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, at most two earlier wires each; wires 0 to 6 the inputs, gate j writes wire 7+j) and the output wire, judged on every input. 21 is the size of the best AND/OR circuit the checker has accepted. A NOT-free circuit of 18 gates with its last gate rewritten through NOTs meets every clause, and so does a circuit whose NOT can be deleted; say which kind yours is.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 101815 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (101815 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 9
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 10 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 9; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 2. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: No AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 20 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 12 vertices with 16 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. This side says the best circuit we know cannot be beaten by one gate: a finite search with a certificate the kernel replays, or an argument by restricting one vertex at a time down to smaller graphs whose sizes are checked. Size: unknown. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
